title: Check lint: flag an entry whose text names a second command or an output claim that belongs to another command, such as `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork runs only the backticked command of a Check entry and applies the entry's expectation ("prints nothing", "exits 0") to that command. Spec drafts often join several commands in one entry, so the expectation of a later command lands on the first one:
- S598 (run ork-20261125-232714-f9a7) went red in round 3 on "- `go test ./...` exits 0, go vet ./... prints nothing, and gofmt -l . prints nothing." go test passed, but ork applied "must print nothing" to it.
- S606 and S622 drafts on 2026-11-27 had "- `go vet ./...` reports nothing, and gofmt -l /home/... prints nothing." and "- `go test ./...` passes; go vet ./... prints nothing; gofmt -l ... prints nothing.", fixed by hand before the start.

ork should flag such an entry in the spec check, the spec draft and ork run (like S563's non-command lint), naming the unbackticked command, so each command gets its own entry.
